solutions.latex:
By the max-flow min-cut theorem, the maximum flow equals the minimum cut capacity.

Every cut capacity is an upper bound on the flow, so the maximum flow cannot exceed the capacity of the given cut, which is 30.

Other cuts may have smaller capacity, so the maximum flow could be less than 30. The given information does not show that the cut shown is the minimum cut.

Hence the maximum flow is 30 or less, which is option C.

The network diagram shows a series of water channels and ponds in a garden. The vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ and $F$ represent six ponds. The edges represent the water channels which connect the ponds. The numbers on the edges indicate the maximum capacity of the channels.

figures.cap: flow network with a dashed cut

parts.latex: Determine the maximum flow of the network.

solutions.latex:
The minimum cut passes through $BD$, $BE$, $CE$ and $CF$.

By the maximum flow minimum cut theorem, the maximum flow equals the value of the minimum cut.
$$\therefore\ \text{Maximum flow} = 275$$
criteria: Identifies a cut, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Weight of cut} &= 200+75+50 \\ &= 325 \end{aligned}$$
This is not equal to the maximum flow of $275$.

Hence the cut is not a minimum cut.

solutions.latex:
The capacity of a cut is the sum of the capacities of the edges that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side. An edge crossing in the opposite direction is not counted.

The cut crosses edges $E$, $I$, $J$ and $H$.

Edges $E$, $J$ and $H$ point from the source side to the sink side, so they are counted. Edge $I$ points back across the cut to the source side, so it is not counted.
$$\text{Capacity} = E + J + H$$
Hence the correct option is C.

By the minimum cut, maximum flow theorem, the maximum flow is $300$ people per hour.

parts.latex:
The flow capacity of water through pipelines, in kL/h, is shown in the network diagram below.

\exfigure{15_q30_1}

A manager determines that the network does not provide sufficient flow capacity and wants to change the direction of flow through one pipe in order to increase the total capacity.

Recommend a pipe in which the flow direction could be reversed to increase the maximum flow capacity of the network. Provide a justification for this recommendation by calculating and comparing maximum flow capacities before and after the adjustment.

solutions.latex:
The maximum flow of the original network is
$$45 + 55 + 70 = 170 \text{ kL/h}$$
If the flow in pipe $BC$ is reversed (from $C$ to $B$), a further $15$ kL/h can flow.
$$170 + 15 = 185 \text{ kL/h}$$
Therefore reverse the direction of pipe $BC$, increasing the maximum flow from $170$ kL/h to $185$ kL/h.
criteria: Identifies reversing $BC$ and the original flow $170$ kL/h, or identifies reversing $BC$ and the new flow $185$ kL/h, or equivalent merit

meta.final: Reverse pipe $BC$, increasing maximum flow from $170$ kL/h to $185$ kL/h.
